earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog refs for tepi1241 are only classification/overview items (Merrifield 1994 bibliography, Garza Cuaron & Lastra 1991, Ethnologue); no grammar or phonology of Tepinapa Chinantec exists.

sources.citation: Lingmex: Bibliografia linguistica de Mexico desde 1970 (El Colegio de Mexico), simple-search API queried for Tepinapa, Petlapa, Lovani, Toavela, Teotalcingo, 'sureste medio', Lalana.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Zero records for every Tepinapa-area name; 'Lalana' returns 3 (Nakamoto 2026 UNAM PhD 'Gramatica del chinanteco de Lalana'; Mugele & Mugele 1976, 1977 primers) -- all Lalana Chinantec (lala1270), not Tepinapa.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Internet Archive full-text search (be-api.us.archive.org/fts) for "Tepinapa" alone and with Chinantec / Petlapa / Rensch / ballistic / Merrifield / 'tone syllable'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonological hit: results are botanical collections (Liebmann), Bevan 1938 travel report, Weitlaner (ed.) 1977 Relatos, mitos y leyendas de la Chinantla (Tepinapa folk texts in Spanish, 1954), print Ethnologues, Grimes 1974 Language 50 (Tepinapa as an intelligibility test center), World Christian Encyclopedia etc.
Only herbarium specimen records for Tepinapa/Petlapa; no thesis or article on the language; Nakamoto's 2026 Lalana grammar not yet deposited.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog, 'OLAC resources in and about the Tepinapa Chinantec language' (as of 2025-02-25, archived copy (Internet Archive, 26 Feb 2025)).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; lists only two records for cte (Glottolog 5.1 and Ethnologue 2018) -- no language description, lexicon or text archived at SIL, AILLA, ELAR or elsewhere.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2016. Ethnologue (web ed.), 'Chinantec, Tepinapa [cte]' (archived copy (Internet Archive, 9 Aug 2016)).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology/stress. Gives locations (San Juan Petlapa municipality: Toavela, Santa Isabel Cajonos, Lovani; Santiago Jocotepec municipality: Linda Vista, San Pedro Tepinapa Comunal/Ejidal) and 'Dialects: None known. 87%-68% intelligibility of Lalana [cnl], 24% of Lealao [cle], 23% of Ozumacin [chz]'.

sources.citation: INALI. 2008. Catalogo de las lenguas indigenas nacionales: variantes linguisticas de Mexico -- chinanteco page, entry 'jujmi (del sureste medio) <chinanteco del sureste medio>' (Internet Archive copy).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; self-designation and locality list only (Petlapa, Toavela, Lovani, Teotalcingo, Tepinapa, Jocotepec..).

sources.citation: Silverman, Daniel. 2006. 'Chinantec: Phonology'. In K. Brown (ed.), Encyclopedia of Language and Linguistics, 2nd ed., 211-213 (held under coma1246).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level only: lists the '14 major languages' (Ojitlan.. Lalana, Lealao, Quiotepec, Comaltepec) -- Tepinapa is not treated as a separate language; general statement that stem complexes are obligatorily stressed and that several languages have ballistic vs controlled stress on stem syllables. No Tepinapa data.

sources.citation: Merrifield, William R. & Calvin R. Rensch (eds.) 1990. Syllables, tone, and verb paradigms (Studies in Chinantec Languages 4). Dallas: SIL -- introduction, scanned pp.5-33 (held under coma1246).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comaltepec/Lealao etc. only; no mention of Tepinapa in the pages read.

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. 1989. An etymological dictionary of the Chinantec languages (Studies in Chinantec Languages 1; SIL Publications in Linguistics 87). Dallas: SIL & UT Arlington.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative Chinantec reference with an introduction on syllable structure, tone and stress across the sampled towns; need to check whether any Tepinapa-area town is among its data points (Silverman's derived 14-language list suggests not). SIL archive PDF exists but sil.org was could not be reached by automated download.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Tepinapa' 0 hits; 'chinanteco' 7 hits (Quiotepec tone/phonation theses, Temextitlan narrative, regional studies) -- nothing on southeastern (Tepinapa/Petlapa) Chinantec.

Nothing; classification (Southern Chinantec, with Lalana and Lealao) and 4 non-descriptive refs (Merrifield 1994 overview, Garza Cuaron & Lastra 1991, Ethnologue 2009, LL-MAP); 0 grammar/phonology/sketch refs.

sources.citation: SIL Mexico (mexico.sil.org) publication search for language code cte; Chinantec family page.
sources.note: Search returns 'no results' for cte; family page mentions only tone in general terms and does not mention Tepinapa.

sources.citation: Nakamoto, Shun. 2026. Gramatica del chinanteco de Lalana. Tesis de doctorado, Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico (committee: Uchihara, Tallman, Beam de Azcona, Swanton).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Newest full grammar of the closest relative (Lalana, 87%-68% intelligibility per Ethnologue); its phonology chapter (tone, ballistic syllables, stress) is the best available proxy and may contain explicit notes on the Tepinapa/Petlapa ('sureste medio') varieties. Found only as a Lingmex record; not yet in TESIUNAM/Repositorio UNAM.

sources.citation: Merrifield, William R. 1994. Progress in Chinantec language studies. In L. Manrique, Y. Lastra & D. Bartholomew (eds.), Panorama de los estudios de las lenguas indigenas de Mexico, Tomo II, 187-236. Quito: Abya-Yala.

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only Glottolog ref; a state-of-the-field survey by the SIL Chinantec coordinator that would say whether any unpublished SIL field notes, word lists or survey phonologies exist for Tepinapa/Petlapa/Toavela and how Tepinapa relates to Lalana.

sources.citation: Egland, Steven (con Doris Bartholomew y Saul Cruz Ramos). 1978 [2nd ed. 1983]. La inteligibilidad interdialectal en Mexico: resultados de algunos sondeos. Mexico: Instituto Linguistico de Verano (Chinantec section; Tepinapa listed as a test center).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open copy online, not downloaded; the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: SIL dialect-intelligibility survey that tested Tepinapa, Petlapa, Toavela, Lovani, Teotalcingo; establishes which described variety (Lalana) Tepinapa groups with, and whether SIL collected Tepinapa word lists; PDF normally open on mexico.sil.

sources.citation: Mugele, Robert Louis. 1982. Tone and ballistic syllable in Lalana Chinantec. Ph.D. dissertation, University of Texas at Austin.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login
sources.note: Dedicated prosodic study of the nearest described variety (Lalana); would supply the stress/ballistic-syllable statement for the Lalana-Tepinapa cluster if Tepinapa is to be covered by proxy (identity caveat: lala1270, not tepi1241).

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. & Carolyn M. Rensch. 1966. The Lalana Chinantec syllable. In A. Pompa y Pompa (ed.), Summa anthropologica en homenaje a Roberto J. Weitlaner, 455-463. Mexico: INAH.

sources.note: Original description of Lalana syllable prosody (ballistic vs controlled stress, tone); proxy for the undescribed Tepinapa variety.
